newsitem.title: USA: USWC gasolines rise with NYMEX, low inventories.
newsitem.headline: USWC gasolines rise with NYMEX, low inventories.

text.p: U.S. West Coast spot gasoline prices advanced Tuesday, following a sharp rise in futures markets and weekly data showing low inventories, traders said.
West Coast spot trade was heavy, brokers said. A CARB-grade gasoline deal was done in Los Angeles at 78.50 cents, with ranges two cents over Monday at 79.50/80.50 cents.
April CARB gasoline deals were heard done between 75.50 and 76.75 cents a gallon, traders said.
NYMEX markets rose on a technical rally and news that some barge traffic was closed on the Mississippi River Tuesday.
April NYMEX gasoline firmed 2.22 cents to 67.48 cents.
Front-month heating oil rose a sharp 1.88 cent-rise to 56.18.

West Coast gasoline inventories dropped 1.2 million barrels last week to 25.7 million, and nationwide, stocks fell 4.3 million, according to a late Tuesday report from the American Petroleum Institute.
Conventional grade gasoline in L.A. was assessed 76.50/77.50 cents a gallon, up 2.50 cents over Monday.
Distillates were flat from Monday in both San Francisco and Los Angeles, traders said.
